---
title: "Commenting out the last step of a pipe swallows the next statement"
ref: PIP-04
categories: [Pipes]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "`[1] 1 2 3`"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2024)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
result <- c(3, 1, 2) |>
  sort() |>
  # rev()

print(result)
```
:::

## Why

R ignores the comment and the blank line. What it reads is a chain ending with `|>`, hence an incomplete statement, which carries on onto the next line of code it finds. The code actually run is `result <- print(sort(c(3, 1, 2)), result)`.

`result` does not exist yet when `print()` evaluates its second argument, hence "object 'result' not found" on a line that seems to merely print a variable just created. If the next statement did not use `result`, the code would run silently, with an absurd result. {magrittr} has the same problem with a trailing `%>%`.

## The fix

Comment out a step in the middle, never the last one, or end every chain with a neutral step such as `identity()` so that everything before it can be commented out.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
result <- c(3, 1, 2) |>
  sort() |>
  # rev() |>
  identity()

print(result)
```
:::
